q: What does Faridabad's engineering cluster use in energy, and what do auto OEMs ask its suppliers for?
title: Faridabad engineering: energy and OEM asks
short: About 12,015 MSMEs, 35% making auto parts, run on grid power with DG sets as backup, plus diesel, furnace oil, LPG, pet coke, wood and gas. The 5,347 units surveyed used 426,167 toe a year. Auto and tractor OEMs ask each vendor for monthly fuel and power, Scope 1 and 2, and a figure per part.
audience: Auto parts, sheet metal, fabrication, forging and heat treatment MSMEs in Faridabad supplying vehicle and tractor OEMs

sections.h: The cluster, from the last full survey (2011 to 12)
ul: About 12,015 MSMEs: 4,612 micro, 7,039 small and 364 medium.
Auto parts make up 35% of units, sheet metal components 14% and fabrication 11%. Castings, forging, heat treatment, electroplating, fasteners, rubber and plastics make up most of the rest.
A large share work as vendors to car, two-wheeler and tractor OEMs.
Energy is just over 2% of manufacturing cost in fabrication units and over 44% in foundries, so the same OEM form means very different work for different vendors.
Grid power from DHBVN runs presses, machine shops and welding. Power cuts mean almost every unit has a DG set, so diesel turns up in nearly every Scope 1 figure.
Furnace oil, LPG, pet coke, wood and piped gas fire furnaces in forging, heat treatment and foundries.
The 5,347 units in the survey used 426,167 toe a year: on average about 80 toe a unit, a rough figure that hides a spread from tiny fabricators to large foundries.
The survey's biggest saving options: switching furnaces from furnace oil to PNG or electric, excess air control, furnace temperature control and inverter welding machines.

sections.h: What the OEM supplier form asks, and where each answer comes from
ol: Electricity in kWh by month: your DHBVN bills.
Diesel for the DG set in litres: fuel purchase slips, less stock in the tank at year end.
Furnace fuels by month: furnace oil, LPG, PNG or pet coke invoices.
Scope 1 and Scope 2 in tonnes CO2e, with the factors named.
Output: parts or tonnes shipped to that OEM, so it can work out a figure per part.
Plans to cut emissions: a fuel switch or furnace upgrade, with dates.

example.title: Worked example: a sheet metal press shop with a paint oven, one month
lines: Grid power: 40,000 kWh x 0.675 kg = 27.0 t CO2 (Scope 2)
DG set: 1,500 L diesel x 2.645 kg = 3.97 t CO2 (Scope 1)
Paint oven: 1,200 kg LPG x 2.98 kg = 3.58 t CO2 (Scope 1)
Total: 34.5 t CO2 for 180 t of pressings shipped, about 0.19 t CO2 per tonne from the plant's own energy
The steel sheet comes on top. At 1.15 t of sheet per tonne of pressings, the mill's figure per tonne of sheet matters far more than your power bill
example.note: Quantities are an example. Factors: CEA grid factor for FY 2025-26 and IPCC 2006 fuel defaults. Use your mill's figure for the sheet; the 1.15 yield is illustrative.

senseible: Upload a year of DHBVN bills, DG diesel slips and furnace fuel invoices, and Senseible returns the monthly Scope 1 and 2 figures an OEM form asks for, each line linked to the bill it came from.
